correctness.rationale: For b>µ the positive predator nullcline is exactly x=(1+y)/λ and prey derivative along it equals −P(y)/λ² with P(y)=y²−[λ−aλ²/(1+λ)]y+(1−λ); all denominators positive. Quadratic signs and discriminant prove exhaustive root counts and exact λ_c,a_f cutoffs. At positive roots det J=µ y P′(y)/[(1+λ)(1+y)], and both diagonal entries are negative for 0<λ<1, so the lower root is a saddle and upper is a sink. The source boundary is also a sink with eigenvalues −1,µ(λ−1)/2. P′′=2 and ∂_aP>0 guarantee a generic fold. A fully rational example and a standalone 600-case checker cross-check the identities. Finite tests are not claimed as proofs of the parameter-uniform result.

originality.rationale: The 2026 originating full text derives a nonmonotone carrying-capacity term and specifically defers equilibrium and stability analysis. Its formula is not an implication of the exact sharp backward-persistence coexistence wedge: elimination on the predator nullcline, discriminant conditions, and Jacobian signs are required. Compared earlier full texts use prescribed logistic growth or separate environmental carrying capacity, not the same coupled rational reaction equation. Indexed related findings involve cooperative hunting or discrete maps rather than this continuum two-state refuge mechanism. Absolute historical priority is not established; one relevant 2019 related full text was inaccessible.

value.rationale: The model paper explicitly points to equilibria/stability as future work and physically motivates prey carrying-capacity feedback from rapid refuge switching. The analysis supplies the exact condition when negative linear predator invasion nevertheless coexists with stable predator persistence, including sharp fold and rational witness. It is not merely an arbitrary numeric slice, generic saddle-node theorem or previously catalogued simple logistic equilibrium; it resolves a structurally motivated subthreshold persistence question for the source reaction model.
